method.source: Actual page-image inspection, not OCR or lexical candidates. All full-page images were rendered from the canonical source PDF with PyMuPDF at 216 dpi and opened individually. Bounded crops are 2x enlargements from those full-page images with base path/hash and pixel bounds recorded.

method.statuses: `partial` means the exact joined scope contains both a represented facet and missing source detail or mixed excluded/in-scope material. `absent` is limited to named source assertions in the complete captured current owner set. `excluded` applies only to full monster profile/stat scope under the documented feature boundary. None implies whole-book completion.

sharedProcedureCensus.summary: The common text limits elemental conjuring by daily frequency, means and elemental type, gives examples using spells, staves and a summoning device, and distinguishes same-type from different-type possibilities.
sharedProcedureCensus.scope: The broad limit is plainly an elemental procedure; the phrase “per means” and its cross-spell/class application are semantically unresolved. No device count or Druid-specific cap is invented.

sharedProcedureCensus.summary: If control concentration fails, the text gives a 75% turn-and-attack branch; a 25% branch immediately returns the elemental to its own plane. It says control cannot be regained and a turned elemental returns to its plane three turns after control is lost.
sharedProcedureCensus.scope: These are conditional on failure to maintain the conjuring party’s control; they are not the PHB separate 5% rebellion check.

sharedProcedureCensus.summary: The conjuring party must remain stationary and avoid physical or mental attack, including missile attack or distraction; only one elemental at a time can be controlled.
sharedProcedureCensus.scope: Generic rule text in the cited source area; no class or exception beyond specifically cited PHB Druid text is inferred.

sharedProcedureCensus.scope: Shared combat rule is recorded as a distinct source clause; it is not transcribed into a new generic rule or inferred from a profile stat block.

sourceRecord.name: Conjure Elemental

fields.Material: Air: burning incense; earth: soft clay; fire: sulfur and phosphorus; water: water and sand

effect: Conjure an air, earth, fire or water elemental, choosing the type when memorizing the spell.
conditions: Fire and water versions also require a substantial source of the appropriate element within range.
Concentrate to control it within 3″ per caster level; wounds or grappling break concentration.
Even with concentration, there is a 5% chance of rebellion at the end of the second round and each later round.
exceptions: An uncontrolled elemental seeks to attack the conjurer, though it does not abandon an ongoing combat to do so.
A water elemental is destroyed if it moves more than 6″ from a body of water.
The source points to protective circles, pentacles and protection from evil as safeguards.

sourceRecord.name: Conjure Fire Elemental
effect: Summons a 16-HD fire elemental 85% of the time; 9% brings 2–4 salamanders, 4% an efreeti, and 2% a 21–24-HD fire elemental.
conditions: Druid needs neither a protective circle nor continuous concentration, and the summoned force does not turn on the druid.
exceptions: Ends by expiry, attack, dispelling or dismiss fire elemental. Only a druid can dismiss the salamanders, efreeti or exceptionally powerful elementals.

exceptions: Travelers cannot detect the true dimensions by ordinary means; a faint magical aura remains, and true seeing reveals the spread-out elemental.

sourceRecord.name: Dust Devil
effect: Summons a weak air elemental: AC 4, 2 HD, movement 18″ and one attack for 1d4 damage. Magic weapons deal it double damage.
Can push back gas and extinguish small nonmagical flames; over loose dust/sand/ash it creates a 30-foot cloud that blinds victims until one round after leaving.
conditions: It follows direction but vanishes if ordered beyond 3″; a caster inside it must save versus spell to preserve concentration even without taking damage.
exceptions: Any creature native to the Elemental Plane of Air, including another dust devil, can dismiss it within 3″; creatures not native to the plane occupied by the caster are unaffected.
Innate magic resistance dispels it after it gets a chance to hit.

elephantSourceProseFacts.summary: Five attack forms are identified (two tusks, trunk and two forefeet). At most two can affect one opponent at a time; six or more man-sized opponents can be engaged. This is bounded to the two named source units, their displayed cross-reference entries, the cited current spell/rule routes and complete captured owner set; it is not a semantic review of every MM profile or page.
limitations: The app has no searchable monster collection; full profile stats/abilities remain excluded by product boundary. This report independently classifies the specific exposed source procedures and economic/service assertions identified above.
Some site “present” topic mentions come from different books (PHB/UA) and are retained as nonjoins; they do not supply MM citations or source values.
The shared MM phrase “per means” remains an actual interpretation boundary, not OCR uncertainty or a guessed spell cap.
No app, source catalog, production citation, or source image catalog was changed; only this new research report was written.
